main_text.p: cùm Apostolus ait 2. Timoth. 3. Omnis scriptura divinitùs inspirata, utilis est ad doctrinam, &c. Item, quòd potest sapientem facere ad salutem: videndum est, quosnam possint sapientes facere, & quibus utilis sit ad doctrinam. Non certè illis, qui hanc scripturam in libris tantùm & cistis, & Musæis tenent, sed nunquam legunt, nunquam audiunt: verùm illis, qui eam legunt, audiunt, intelligunt, fide recipiunt. Ideo subiecit Apostolus, dicendo: Quæ te possunt facere sapientem per fidem, quæ est in Christo Iesu. Item Rom. 1. Euangelium est potentia Dei in salutem omni credenti. Fides autem est ex auditu. Rom.10.

Quæstio igitur hæc proponitur: An officium sit cuiusq; Christiani, imò cuiusvis hominis, operam dare sacris Literis, non solùm audiendis, cùm explicantur in Templo & in schola, sed etiam domi legendis & scrutandis, nec ne.

Papistæ permulti, præsertim hoc tempore, negant permittendum esse cuique legere scripturas, vt mulieribus, Laicis, indoctis, pueris, militibus, plebeis: Hoc esse officium Ecclesiasticorum & Theologorum, doctorumq; virorum. Quas adferant rationes, ad extremum breviter recitabo & refutabo. Sententiam nostram continet hæc
main_text.head: THESIS.

page.notes: The running head is printed "SCRIPTVRA." and is kept as printed. The page number "305" is in old-style figures and is only approximate. The signature "V" at lower left is doubtful. The opening word of the Quæstio paragraph has a swash form, read as "An" with doubt. The reference "2. Timoth. 3." and the Rom. references are read as printed but may be in old figures. The text of the first paragraph is copied from the scan, not from the known Vulgate wording.
